Container.Name: kanidm
Container.Overview:
Kanidm is a modern, secure identity management server written in Rust. It provides OAuth2 / OpenID Connect single sign-on, passkeys (WebAuthn), TOTP, a read-only LDAPS gateway, RADIUS (separate container), SSH key distribution and Unix/PAM logins, all from one small service with its own web portal.
**Before the first start**
Kanidm only speaks HTTPS, even behind a reverse proxy, and will not start without a certificate.
1. Set **Domain** and **Origin** below. They must match (`idm.example.com` with `https://idm.example.com`). The domain is baked into passkeys and OAuth2 and is hard to change later; read https://kanidm.github.io/kanidm/stable/choosing_a_domain_name.html first. 2. Certificate, pick one: - Your own: put `chain.pem` (full chain) and `key.pem` in `/mnt/user/appdata/kanidm`, for example a wildcard Let's Encrypt certificate copied from your reverse proxy. - Self-signed (fine behind a reverse proxy). Run this once in the Unraid terminal, using your own domain and origin:
`docker run --rm -v /mnt/user/appdata/kanidm:/data -e KANIDM_DOMAIN=idm.example.com -e KANIDM_ORIGIN=https://idm.example.com -e KANIDM_TLS_CHAIN=/data/chain.pem -e KANIDM_TLS_KEY=/data/key.pem -e KANIDM_DB_PATH=/data/kanidm.db kanidm/server:latest kanidmd cert-generate`
3. Start the container and create the two break-glass admin passwords:
`docker exec -it kanidm kanidmd recover-account admin` `docker exec -it kanidm kanidmd recover-account idm_admin`
`admin` manages server settings and `idm_admin` manages people and groups. The image is minimal and has no shell, so the Unraid Console button will not work; use `docker exec -it kanidm kanidmd ...` as shown. Day-to-day work uses the `kanidm` CLI (https://kanidm.github.io/kanidm/stable/installing_client_tools.html), e.g. `kanidm person create`, then `kanidm person credential create-reset-token`.
**Reverse proxy:** proxy to `https://YOUR-SERVER-IP:8443` (HTTPS backend; skip verification when the certificate is self-signed). To log real client IPs, add an `http_client_address_info` section with `x-forward-for` set to your proxy IP in `/data/server.toml` (see the example config linked below).
**Optional settings:** every option can be set with a `KANIDM_*` variable or in `/data/server.toml` (variables win). Enable LDAPS by adding the variable `KANIDM_LDAPBINDADDRESS` = `0.0.0.0:3636` (the LDAPS port is already mapped). Reference: https://github.com/kanidm/kanidm/blob/master/examples/server_container.toml
**Updates:** Kanidm only supports upgrading one minor version at a time (1.11 to 1.12 to 1.13). If you update rarely, pin the tag (e.g. `kanidm/server:1.12.1`) and step through each release. Run `docker exec -it kanidm kanidmd domain upgrade-check` before upgrading. Online backups are written daily to /data/backups.
**Hardening:** the image runs as root by default. To use a dedicated user, add `--user 4389:4389` (any free UID) to Extra Parameters and `chown -R 4389:4389 /mnt/user/appdata/kanidm` first (see the security hardening chapter).

Container.Requires: A domain name with an HTTPS certificate (or a self-signed one generated with kanidmd cert-generate, see Overview)

Config.Name: HTTPS Port
Config.Description: Web portal, OAuth2/OIDC and API (HTTPS only).

Config.Name: LDAPS Port
Config.Description: Read-only LDAPS gateway. Only active after you set KANIDM_LDAPBINDADDRESS (see Overview).

Config.Name: Data
Config.Description: Database, certificates (chain.pem/key.pem), optional server.toml and online backups.

Config.Name: Domain
Config.Description: Kanidm domain name, e.g. idm.example.com. Choose carefully: changing it breaks passkeys and OAuth2 clients.

Config.Name: Origin
Config.Description: Public HTTPS URL users and OAuth2 clients use. Must be https:// and match the domain.

Config.Name: TLS Chain
Config.Description: Full certificate chain (PEM) inside the container.

Config.Name: Bind Address
Config.Description: HTTPS listen address inside the container.

Config.Name: Database FS Type
Config.Description: Set zfs when appdata is on a ZFS pool, to tune the page size.
